nodes.label: Axios Instance baseURL http://localhost:5139/api
nodes.rationale: Backend base URL is hardcoded to the local ASP.NET Core dev host instead of an env var, coupling every page's HTTP traffic to a single non-configurable origin.

nodes.label: Request Interceptor Bearer Token Injection
nodes.rationale: Auth is attached centrally in one interceptor reading localStorage['spa_token'] so no page has to know about JWT handling; the trade-off is an implicit contract with useAuthStore over the raw storage key rather than an explicit dependency.

nodes.label: useAuthStore (Zustand auth store)
nodes.rationale: Store state is seeded synchronously from localStorage at module init so a page refresh keeps the session without an async rehydration step; the cost is a JSON.parse at import time that will throw on corrupted storage.

nodes.label: User model (id, fullName, email, role, loyaltyPoints)
nodes.norm_label: user model (id, fullname, email, role, loyaltypoints)

nodes.label: Role Model: Customer | Staff | Admin | SuperAdmin
nodes.norm_label: role model: customer | staff | admin | superadmin

nodes.label: localStorage Session Keys (spa_token, spa_user)
nodes.rationale: Session is persisted under two well-known localStorage keys shared by the auth store and the axios interceptor; chosen for simplicity over a cookie/httpOnly approach, at the cost of XSS exposure and a stringly-typed contract duplicated across two modules.

nodes.label: 3-Step Booking Wizard (Service+Staff / Date+Slot / Review)
nodes.rationale: Booking is split into three guarded steps with Next disabled until a selection exists, so an invalid payload can never reach POST /bookings; step state is local component state rather than routed URL state, so a refresh loses wizard progress.

nodes.label: Deep-link Preselection (?serviceId, ?staffId)
nodes.rationale: Services and Staff pages hand off a chosen entity through query params so the wizard opens prefilled; note the preselection match only runs inside the API-failure fallback branch, not on the successful response path.

nodes.label: Booking Payload (customerId, serviceId, staffId, date, timeSlot, notes)
nodes.norm_label: booking payload (customerid, serviceid, staffid, date, timeslot, notes)

nodes.label: Any-Staff Auto-Assign Default (falls back to 'stf-1')
nodes.rationale: Choosing 'Any Staff' sends a hardcoded 'stf-1' instead of letting the backend auto-assign, so the UI's stated auto-assign promise is not actually delegated to the server.

nodes.label: Mock Availability Slots (setTimeout stub)
nodes.rationale: Time slots are produced by a 400ms setTimeout over a fixed array; no availability endpoint is called, so date/service/staff selection has no real effect on offered slots.

nodes.label: Loyalty Rules: +10 pts per completed booking, 100 pts = free service
nodes.rationale: A flat 10 points per completed reservation with a 100-point free-treatment threshold keeps the reward math trivial for customers and makes the progress bar a simple percentage; it ignores service price, so a $45 blowdry earns the same as a $110 body wrap.
nodes.norm_label: loyalty rules: +10 pts per completed booking, 100 pts = free service

nodes.label: BookingItem view model (serviceName, staffName, date, timeSlot, status, price)
nodes.norm_label: bookingitem view model (servicename, staffname, date, timeslot, status, price)

nodes.label: Booking Status Lifecycle (Pending/Confirmed/Completed/Cancelled/NoShow)
nodes.rationale: The same five-value status union is redeclared inline in MyBookings and AdminBookings rather than imported from a shared type, so the customer and admin views can silently drift from each other and from the backend enum.

nodes.label: Cancellation Policy (2-hour minimum notice)
nodes.rationale: The 2-hour notice rule is only stated in a window.confirm string on the client; nothing here enforces it, so the rule must be validated server-side to mean anything.

nodes.label: Upcoming vs Past Tab Split (date + status derived)
nodes.norm_label: upcoming vs past tab split (date + status derived)

nodes.label: Service Category Taxonomy (8 categories)
nodes.rationale: The category list (HaircutStyling, FacialSkincare, MassageTherapy, NailCare, BodyTreatments, Waxing, MakeupBeauty, EyelashEyebrow) is duplicated as a const array in Services.tsx and as <option> values in AdminServices.tsx, mirroring a backend enum with no single shared source.

nodes.label: Waitlist Status Lifecycle (Waiting/Offered/Booked/Expired)
nodes.rationale: The Offered state carries a 24-hour claim window, which is what the backend waitlist-expiration background job exists to enforce; the frontend only renders the countdown message.

nodes.label: Join Waitlist Submission (client-generated entry object)
nodes.rationale: The POST body is the fully-formed client view model including a client-invented id and status, instead of a minimal command (serviceId + preferredDate); the server's own id is never read back.

nodes.label: Admin Analytics Page (Recharts)
nodes.rationale: Revenue and category charts are driven entirely by module-level constant arrays; there is no analytics endpoint call at all, so this page is presentational scaffolding awaiting a data source.

nodes.label: Status->Endpoint Map (confirm/complete/cancel/no-show)
nodes.rationale: A record maps each target status to its own REST action URL rather than PUTting a status field, keeping transitions as explicit server commands; note Cancelled deliberately routes to the shared customer /bookings/{id}/cancel route instead of an /admin one.

nodes.label: Admin Dashboard Overview Page
nodes.rationale: KPI tiles and today's timeline are hardcoded literals with no API call; the page functions as a navigation hub into the other admin screens.

nodes.label: Active/Off-Duty Toggle (local state only)
nodes.rationale: toggleStatus mutates React state with no PUT, and 'Add Staff Member' / 'Edit Hours' are alert() stubs, so staff administration is not yet wired to the backend.

nodes.label: Twilio SMS + SendGrid Email Slot-Offer Notification
nodes.rationale: Offering a freed slot is described as dispatching both an SMS (Twilio) and an email (SendGrid) with a 24h confirm window; the admin handler currently only flips local status and alerts, so the dispatch is asserted in copy, not performed.
nodes.norm_label: twilio sms + sendgrid email slot-offer notification

nodes.label: Offline Mock-Data Fallback Pattern (.catch -> seed demo data)
nodes.rationale: Every data-fetching page swallows the API error and substitutes a hardcoded demo dataset so the UI is always demonstrable without a running backend; the trade-off is that genuine outages, auth failures and 500s are invisible to the user and to QA, and the mocked ids (srv-1, stf-1) leak into real POST payloads.
nodes.norm_label: offline mock-data fallback pattern (.catch -> seed demo data)

nodes.label: Optimistic Mutation Pattern (update state, ignore API failure)
nodes.rationale: Cancel, leave-waitlist, service create/update/delete and admin status changes all mutate local state whether the request resolves or rejects (several use .catch(() => {})), so the screen can report success for a write the server refused.
nodes.norm_label: optimistic mutation pattern (update state, ignore api failure)

nodes.label: Shared Demo Dataset (services srv-1..6, staff stf-1..4, Iraqi salon personas)
nodes.rationale: The same fixture names, ids, prices and durations are copy-pasted across Booking, Services, Staff, MyBookings, Waitlist and every admin page, forming an undeclared shared fixture that must be edited in eight places to stay consistent.
nodes.norm_label: shared demo dataset (services srv-1..6, staff stf-1..4, iraqi salon personas)

nodes.label: i18n Translation Keys (react-i18next t())
nodes.rationale: Public customer pages route labels through t() for Arabic/English support, while every admin page hardcodes English strings — localization is intentionally scoped to the customer-facing surface.

nodes.label: Availability Slots Endpoint (unwired / missing)
nodes.rationale: The comment 'Simulate / fetch availability slots from backend' marks an intended endpoint that was never called; this is the largest gap between the booking UI and the backend.

nodes.label: React + TypeScript + Vite Template
nodes.rationale: The README is still the unmodified Vite scaffold, so it documents the toolchain (Vite HMR, @vitejs/plugin-react with Oxc, or plugin-react-swc with SWC) rather than the spa reservation app itself.

nodes.label: React Compiler (deliberately disabled)
nodes.rationale: React Compiler is not enabled in this template because of its impact on dev and build performance; enabling it is left to the app author.

nodes.label: Oxlint Configuration (type-aware rules via oxlint-tsgolint)
nodes.rationale: Type-aware lint rules are opt-in for production apps because they require the extra oxlint-tsgolint package and .oxlintrc.json typeAware flag; the recommended rules are react/rules-of-hooks and react/only-export-components.

nodes.label: API Composition Root (Program.cs)
nodes.rationale: Single minimal-hosting entry point wires CORS (AllowAll), Swagger+Bearer security definition, JWT bearer validation, Infrastructure DI, MediatR assembly scan, startup DB seeding, exception middleware and Hangfire recurring jobs; ordering is deliberate - ExceptionHandlingMiddleware is registered before Swagger/auth so it wraps the whole pipeline.

nodes.label: API Application Settings
nodes.rationale: Holds DefaultConnection (LocalDB) and JwtSettings (Secret/Issuer/Audience/ExpiryMinutes); the JWT secret is committed in plaintext, which is acceptable only for local development.

nodes.label: ExceptionHandlingMiddleware
nodes.rationale: Maps exception types to HTTP status codes (InvalidOperationException->400, UnauthorizedAccessException->401, else 500) and always serializes the stack trace into the response body, which leaks internals outside development.

nodes.label: AuthController
nodes.rationale: Google login is simulated - the Google token is never validated and a random external id is minted per call, so every login creates a new Customer; marked in-source as a demonstration stub.

nodes.label: BookingsController
nodes.rationale: Only controller that is [Authorize]d and the only one that goes through MediatR; it binds command records directly as request bodies instead of separate API DTOs.

nodes.label: Application Class1 Placeholder
nodes.rationale: Empty template class left over from `dotnet new classlib`; referenced by nothing and safe to delete.

nodes.label: IBookingReminderJob
nodes.rationale: Abstraction lives in Application so the API can schedule jobs without referencing Infrastructure; Hangfire resolves the concrete implementation from DI at execution time.

nodes.label: CreateBookingCommand
nodes.rationale: Used as the MediatR assembly marker type in Program.cs, so moving or renaming this record silently changes which assembly is scanned for handlers.

nodes.label: CreateBookingCommandHandler
nodes.rationale: Carries a `// Basic validation...` placeholder and injects no service/staff repositories despite importing those namespaces - double-booking and staff-availability checks are not enforced here.

nodes.label: CreateBookingCommandValidator
nodes.rationale: FluentValidation rules (non-empty ids, date not in the past, start<end, notes<=500) exist but no AddValidatorsFromAssembly / ValidationBehavior pipeline registration was found, so the validator appears never to run.

nodes.label: PagedResult<T>
nodes.rationale: Generic pagination envelope with computed TotalPages/HasPreviousPage/HasNextPage; guards division by zero when PageSize is 0.

nodes.label: CQRS via MediatR Dispatch
nodes.rationale: Write-side booking operations are modelled as request records handled one-per-file so the API layer stays thin and transaction boundaries live in the Application layer; MediatR is registered by assembly scan from CreateBookingCommand's assembly.

nodes.label: Controller-to-Repository Direct Access
nodes.rationale: Read-only public catalog endpoints (services, staff, customer lookup) bypass MediatR and inject domain repositories straight into the controller, trading architectural consistency for fewer files on simple queries.

nodes.label: JWT Bearer Authentication
nodes.rationale: Symmetric HMAC-SHA256 tokens minted by AuthController and validated by the JwtBearer handler configured in Program.cs; both sides read the same JwtSettings section, so issuer/audience/secret must stay in sync.

nodes.label: Centralized Exception-to-HTTP Mapping
nodes.rationale: One middleware converts unhandled exceptions to a uniform JSON error envelope so handlers can throw instead of returning result objects.

nodes.label: Hangfire Recurring Job Scheduling
nodes.rationale: Three recurring jobs (reminder-24h daily, reminder-1h hourly, waitlist-expire daily) are declared imperatively at startup against an interface so schedules are versioned with the code; the dashboard at /hangfire is mounted without any authorization filter.

nodes.label: Offset Pagination Envelope
nodes.rationale: Repositories return an (items, totalCount) tuple and controllers wrap it with PagedResult<T>.Create, keeping paging metadata computation in one place.

nodes.label: Class1 (empty template placeholder)
nodes.rationale: Leftover from the `dotnet new classlib` template; never referenced by any domain type. Dead code that should be deleted.

nodes.label: BookingCompleted domain event (carries LoyaltyPointsEarned)
nodes.rationale: Unlike the other three events it carries a payload value (LoyaltyPointsEarned) so the subscriber that credits the customer does not have to re-derive the award amount.

nodes.label: LoyaltyTransaction (child entity, signed ledger line)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately an Entity, not an AggregateRoot, and has no repository of its own: it is only reachable through the Customer aggregate.

nodes.label: INotificationRepository (does not extend IRepository<T>)
nodes.rationale: Declared standalone rather than as IRepository<Notification> because IRepository<T> is constrained to AggregateRoot and Notification derives from Entity; it exposes only the outbox-poll surface (GetPending/Add/Update).

nodes.label: Booking status transition invariants (guarded state machine)
nodes.rationale: Every mutator re-checks the current status and throws InvalidOperationException rather than silently no-op'ing, so illegal transitions surface as errors. Legal edges: Create->Pending; Pending->Confirmed; Confirmed->Completed; Confirmed->NoShow; Pending|NoShow->Cancelled. Completed and Cancelled are terminal. Note the asymmetry: NoShow is reachable but is not blocked from Cancel, and no transition exists out of NoShow otherwise.
nodes.norm_label: booking status transition invariants (guarded state machine)

nodes.label: Two-hour cancellation cutoff invariant
nodes.rationale: Cancel() refuses when Slot.StartDateTime minus UtcNow is under 2 hours, protecting the staff member's held time. The rule is hard-coded in the aggregate (not configurable) and, because the subtraction is signed, it also blocks cancelling any booking whose start time has already passed.

nodes.label: Flat 10-point award on booking completion
nodes.rationale: Complete() hard-codes LoyaltyPointsEarned = 10 — a flat per-visit award, independent of SalonService.Price or DurationMinutes. The Booking only records the amount and publishes it; it never touches Customer.LoyaltyPoints itself, so the actual credit must happen in a BookingCompleted handler outside the domain layer.

nodes.label: DDD aggregate root vs child entity split
nodes.rationale: Booking, Customer and SalonService derive from AggregateRoot (and so are the only types IRepository<T> accepts); LoyaltyTransaction and Notification derive from Entity and are reached through their owner or a bespoke repository.
nodes.norm_label: ddd aggregate root vs child entity split

nodes.label: Cross-aggregate references held as bare Guids
nodes.rationale: Booking stores CustomerId/StaffId/ServiceId (and LoyaltyTransaction/Notification store CustomerId/BookingId) as plain Guids with no navigation properties, keeping each aggregate independently loadable and transactionally separate. The cost is that no referential invariant is enforced inside the domain.
nodes.norm_label: cross-aggregate references held as bare guids

nodes.label: Private parameterless constructor for EF Core materialization
nodes.rationale: Each persisted class exposes only a static factory plus a private ctor (commented `// EF Core` on Booking) so ORM rehydration works without opening a public constructor that would let callers build invalid state.
nodes.norm_label: private parameterless constructor for ef core materialization

nodes.label: Slot overlap test (half-open interval double-booking check)
nodes.rationale: OverlapsWith uses strict inequalities on both sides, so back-to-back slots that merely touch at an endpoint are NOT overlapping — appointments can be scheduled contiguously. The check lives on the value object, but nothing in the Booking aggregate calls it, so conflict prevention has to be orchestrated by an application service over the repository.
nodes.norm_label: slot overlap test (half-open interval double-booking check)

nodes.label: Loyalty points mechanics (balance plus signed ledger)
nodes.rationale: AwardLoyaltyPoints adds a positive PointsDelta row and DeductLoyaltyPoints adds the negated value, so the denormalized LoyaltyPoints running total should always equal the sum of the ledger. The only invariant guarded is non-negative balance on deduction (throws on insufficient points); awards accept any value, including zero or negative.
nodes.norm_label: loyalty points mechanics (balance plus signed ledger)

nodes.label: External identity mapping (ExternalAuthId + AuthProvider)
nodes.rationale: Customer holds no password: identity is a (provider, external id) pair set at creation and never updated by UpdateProfile, so authentication stays entirely outside the domain.

nodes.label: Notification delivery status and retry counter
nodes.rationale: Status is a magic string ("Pending"/"Sent"/"Failed") rather than an enum — unlike BookingStatus — and MarkFailed increments RetryCount without any max-attempt guard, so a poller draining GetPendingAsync could retry indefinitely; MarkSent/MarkFailed also impose no ordering guard, so a sent notification can be marked failed afterwards.
nodes.norm_label: notification delivery status and retry counter

nodes.label: Bilingual Arabic/English catalog fields
nodes.rationale: Names and descriptions are duplicated as *Ar/*En columns instead of a translation table; Arabic is the required pair (NameAr non-null) matching Customer.PreferredLanguage defaulting to "ar".

nodes.label: Soft deactivation instead of deletion (IsActive)
nodes.rationale: Activate/Deactivate flip an IsActive flag defaulting to true rather than removing the row, so historic bookings that reference a retired ServiceId still resolve; the repository's Active/PagedActive queries are the read-side counterpart.

nodes.label: Entity (domain base class)
nodes.rationale: Every domain entity gets an identity (Guid, generated client-side at construction) and an in-memory domain-event buffer, so aggregates can record side effects without knowing about infrastructure or a dispatcher.

nodes.label: AggregateRoot (marker base class)
nodes.rationale: Empty subclass of Entity used purely as a type-level marker: it is the generic constraint that keeps IRepository<T> from being opened over non-root entities such as WorkingSchedule or TimeOff.

nodes.label: IDomainEvent (marker interface)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately empty marker so the Domain layer carries no MediatR/infrastructure dependency; event dispatch is adapted in Infrastructure.

nodes.label: IRepository<T> generic repository contract
nodes.rationale: Repository interfaces live in Domain (constrained to AggregateRoot) so persistence can be inverted; notably it has no Save/Commit member, which is delegated to IUnitOfWork.

nodes.label: ValueObject base record
nodes.rationale: Implemented as an abstract C# record rather than a hand-written equality base class, so structural equality and immutability come from the language instead of GetEqualityComponents boilerplate.

nodes.label: StaffMember.IsAvailableOn (availability check)
nodes.rationale: Three-gate availability predicate: any TimeOff on the date blocks the whole day, the matching WorkingSchedule must exist and not be IsOff, and the requested window must sit inside [StartTime, EndTime]. It deliberately does NOT consult existing bookings, so the no-double-booking rule must be enforced by a separate collision check outside the aggregate.

nodes.label: TimeOff entity
nodes.rationale: Time off is whole-day only (DateOnly, no time range), which is why IsAvailableOn can short-circuit on a simple date match.

nodes.label: WorkingSchedule entity
nodes.rationale: Keyed by DayOfWeek rather than a concrete date: the weekly recurring pattern is the source of truth for slot generation, and IsOff models a closed weekday without deleting the row.

nodes.label: IWaitlistRepository
nodes.rationale: Its three query methods exist to serve three distinct flows: customer portal (GetByCustomerIdAsync), cancellation fan-out (GetWaitingByServiceAsync) and the Hangfire expiry job (GetExpiredOffersAsync).

nodes.label: WaitlistEntry aggregate root
nodes.rationale: Preferences (staff, date) are nullable so an entry can be broad or specific; CreatedAt gives FIFO ordering for the 'first matching customer' rule and OfferedAt starts the acceptance clock. State transitions are unguarded one-liners (Offer/MarkBooked/Expire) with no legal-transition check, unlike Booking which throws on invalid transitions.

nodes.label: BookingTests (Booking aggregate unit tests)
nodes.rationale: Asserts five domain behaviours: Create defaults Status to Pending, Create raises exactly one BookingCreated domain event, Confirm moves to Confirmed, Cancel succeeds >2h before the slot and throws InvalidOperationException matching '*2 hours*' inside the window, and Complete awards exactly 10 LoyaltyPointsEarned while moving to Completed.

nodes.label: CustomerTests (loyalty behaviour unit tests)
nodes.rationale: Pins the loyalty ledger invariant: awarding points both increments the balance and appends a LoyaltyTransaction with the matching PointsDelta, and deducting more than the balance throws InvalidOperationException matching '*Insufficient*' rather than going negative.

nodes.label: CreateBookingCommandHandlerTests
nodes.rationale: Uses Moq over IBookingRepository and IUnitOfWork to assert the handler's orchestration contract rather than persistence: AddAsync exactly once, SaveChangesAsync exactly once, non-empty returned id. This is the test that proves commit is the handler's responsibility, not the repository's.

nodes.label: UnitTest1 (empty domain test scaffold)
nodes.rationale: Empty xunit template class left over from `dotnet new xunit`; asserts nothing and should be removed now that real test classes exist.

nodes.label: UnitTest1 (empty application test scaffold)
nodes.rationale: Empty xunit template class left over from project scaffolding; asserts nothing.

nodes.label: SPA Salon Reservation System Design Spec
nodes.rationale: Single source of intent for the Ireq SPA Salon platform: .NET 8 DDD backend + React 18 SPA + SQL Server, bilingual AR/EN, social login, multi-channel notifications, loyalty and waitlist. Phase 1 explicitly excludes payments, native apps, multi-branch, video consultation and inventory to keep the first release shippable.
nodes.norm_label: spa salon reservation system design spec

nodes.label: Clean Architecture with DDD layering
nodes.rationale: Four layers (API / Application / Domain / Infrastructure) with the hard rule that Domain holds aggregates, value objects, domain events and repository interfaces and has NO infrastructure dependencies. This is why SharedKernel's IDomainEvent and ValueObject are empty/minimal markers and why IRepository lives in Domain while EF Core implementations live in Infrastructure.

nodes.label: CQRS via MediatR in the Application layer
nodes.rationale: Application layer is defined as CQRS (MediatR) plus DTOs, FluentValidation validators and AutoMapper, so each use case is a command/query handler that owns its own transaction rather than a service class shared across endpoints.
nodes.norm_label: cqrs via mediatr in the application layer

nodes.label: Feature-Sliced frontend architecture
nodes.rationale: Feature folders colocate components, hooks and API calls by domain area, mirroring the backend's bounded contexts so a change to one context touches one folder on each side.

nodes.label: Bookings bounded context
nodes.rationale: Declared the core context: Booking aggregate root, BookingSlot value object, five domain events (Created/Confirmed/Cancelled/Completed/NoShow) and three business rules — no double-booking, slots aligned to staff working hours, 2h minimum cancellation notice.

nodes.label: Services bounded context
nodes.rationale: SalonService carries paired NameAr/NameEn and DescriptionAr/DescriptionEn columns plus IsActive soft-delete, and is partitioned by eight fixed categories from HaircutStyling to EyelashEyebrow.

nodes.label: Staff bounded context
nodes.rationale: StaffMember is the aggregate root with WorkingSchedule and TimeOff as child entities, and specialties are modelled as SpecialtyServiceIds (id references) rather than an entity relation so Staff stays independent of the Services context.

nodes.label: Customers bounded context
nodes.rationale: Customer stores PreferredLanguage plus ExternalAuthId/Provider (no local password), and loyalty is an append-only LoyaltyTransaction ledger alongside the denormalised LoyaltyPoints balance so history is auditable.

nodes.label: Notifications bounded context
nodes.rationale: Notification is persisted per attempt with Channel, Type, Status, SentAt and Error so delivery failures across SendGrid/Twilio SMS/WhatsApp/web-push are retryable rather than fire-and-forget; reminder jobs are scheduled at the moment a booking is confirmed.

nodes.label: Waitlist bounded context
nodes.rationale: WaitlistEntry is its own aggregate root holding CustomerId, ServiceId, PreferredStaffId and PreferredDate, so demand for a fully booked slot is captured without creating a phantom Booking.

nodes.label: Identity and auth context
nodes.rationale: ASP.NET Core Identity plus Google/Facebook OAuth with short-lived JWTs (15min access, 7d refresh) and four roles (Customer/Staff/Admin/SuperAdmin); social-only login removes password storage from scope.

nodes.label: Booking status state machine
nodes.rationale: Pending to Confirmed, then one of Completed, Cancelled or NoShow. Bookings start unconfirmed so an admin (or an availability re-check) gates them, and the three terminal states let analytics separate genuine cancellations from no-shows.

nodes.label: Waitlist status state machine
nodes.rationale: Waiting to Offered, then Booked or Expired. The intermediate Offered state exists so a freed slot is reserved for one customer at a time instead of racing the whole waitlist.

nodes.label: No overlapping bookings per staff member
nodes.rationale: A staff member cannot hold overlapping bookings; this is a cross-aggregate invariant (it needs the set of a staff member's bookings), so it cannot be enforced inside StaffMember or a single Booking instance and must live in a query/handler-level collision check.
nodes.norm_label: no overlapping bookings per staff member

nodes.label: Two-hour minimum cancellation notice
nodes.rationale: Cancellations inside two hours of the appointment are rejected, protecting staff from unrecoverable idle time; admins may still override via the admin panel.

nodes.label: Slot generation from staff working hours
nodes.rationale: Availability is derived, never stored: slots are generated from each staff member's WorkingSchedule at 30-minute intervals, widened when a service exceeds 30 minutes, so changing working hours instantly changes offered slots.
nodes.norm_label: slot generation from staff working hours

nodes.label: Loyalty points earning and redemption rule
nodes.rationale: 10 points per COMPLETED booking (explicitly not on confirmation, so no-shows and cancellations cannot farm points) and 100 points redeem for one admin-defined free service.
nodes.norm_label: loyalty points earning and redemption rule

nodes.label: Waitlist offer and expiry window
nodes.rationale: An offer is made to the first matching customer who then has 24h to accept, while a daily Hangfire job expires entries older than 48h; together they stop a freed slot being held hostage by an unresponsive customer.

nodes.label: Cancellation-triggered waitlist matching
nodes.rationale: When a booking is cancelled the system scans the waitlist for matching entries and notifies them via the WaitlistAvailable notification type, recycling the freed capacity automatically instead of leaving the slot to be rediscovered by browsing.

nodes.label: Admin override of business rules
nodes.rationale: Admins can override any business rule from the admin panel — an explicit escape hatch so real-world salon exceptions do not require a code change, at the cost of invariants not being absolute at the domain layer.

nodes.label: Hangfire background job schedule
nodes.rationale: Four recurring jobs (24h reminders daily at 8 AM, 1h reminders hourly, waitlist expiry daily, notification retry every 15 min) run in-process with SQL Server storage, avoiding a separate worker deployment in Phase 1.

nodes.label: Calendar-first booking flow
nodes.rationale: A single-page funnel — FullCalendar month view, click a date, slide-in slot panel, service picker, auto-suggested or manual staff, review and confirm — chosen so the customer never leaves the page and sees availability before committing to a service.

nodes.label: Bilingual AR/EN with RTL layout
nodes.rationale: i18next ar/en namespaces with a dir="rtl" toggle on the root element and RTL-aware calendar and form layouts; content that is genuinely per-language (service names, descriptions) is duplicated in the schema rather than translated at runtime.

nodes.label: Dark glassmorphism visual theme
nodes.rationale: Deep charcoal background with electric purple to magenta gradients, translucent blurred cards, Cairo for Arabic and Inter for English, and Framer Motion transitions — a luxury-salon register chosen to differentiate from utilitarian booking tools.

nodes.label: Phase 1 scope boundary
nodes.rationale: Online payments, native mobile apps, multi-branch/franchise, video consultation and inventory are all deferred; deployment is also out of scope. This is why Booking carries no payment state and no branch/tenant discriminator anywhere in the domain model.

nodes.label: Infrastructure Class1 Placeholder
nodes.rationale: Empty class left over from the `dotnet new classlib` template; no references anywhere in the solution, kept only because nothing pruned it.

nodes.label: AddInfrastructure Composition Root
nodes.rationale: Single extension method acts as the Infrastructure composition root so the API project never references concrete repositories, preserving the Clean Architecture dependency rule.

nodes.label: EF Core In-Memory Database Provider
nodes.rationale: UseInMemoryDatabase("SpaReservationDb") chosen so the app runs with zero external database setup; data is volatile per process, which is why DbSeeder must re-seed on every startup and why relational features (precision, cascade, owned columns) are configured but never actually enforced.

nodes.label: Hangfire In-Memory Storage and Server
nodes.rationale: Hangfire configured with UseInMemoryStorage plus AddHangfireServer, so the job scheduler is in-process and job history dies with the process; matches the demo posture of the EF in-memory provider but means recurring jobs are re-registered at each boot.

nodes.label: Scoped Repository and UnitOfWork Lifetime
nodes.rationale: Every repository, IUnitOfWork and IBookingReminderJob registered AddScoped so they share one ApplicationDbContext change-tracker per request/job scope; Hangfire jobs must therefore run inside an explicit service scope.

nodes.label: Hangfire Recurring Job Schedule (24h / 1h / waitlist)
nodes.rationale: Jobs are bound to IBookingReminderJob by interface (not concrete class) so Hangfire resolves them from DI per execution: reminder-24h daily, reminder-1h hourly, waitlist-expire daily. The recurrence itself is declared at API startup, not in Infrastructure.

nodes.label: BookingReminderJob (Hangfire worker)
nodes.rationale: Bypasses the repository abstraction and talks to ApplicationDbContext directly, unlike NotificationJobs; simpler for bulk LINQ queries but couples the job to EF Core.

nodes.label: Send24hRemindersAsync
nodes.rationale: Selects Confirmed bookings whose owned Slot.Date equals tomorrow and emits an SMS BookingReminder24h notification already marked Sent; there is no idempotency guard, so a second daily run would duplicate notifications.

nodes.label: Send1hRemindersAsync
nodes.rationale: Computes nextHour only for logging and filters on Slot.Date == today, so every confirmed booking of the day gets a Push reminder on each hourly run rather than only those starting within the hour.

nodes.label: ExpireWaitlistEntriesAsync
nodes.rationale: Expires Offered waitlist entries older than 48 hours using CreatedAt as the clock; mutates tracked aggregates in place and relies on the DbContext change tracker rather than a repository Update call.

nodes.label: INotificationJobs
nodes.rationale: Abstraction declared inside Infrastructure rather than Application (unlike IBookingReminderJob), and never registered in AddInfrastructure, so it is currently unresolvable from DI.

nodes.label: NotificationJobs
nodes.rationale: Repository-based sibling of BookingReminderJob: drains pending notifications through INotificationRepository, keeping EF out of the job body.

nodes.label: ProcessPendingNotificationsAsync
nodes.rationale: Delivery is simulated: it simply calls MarkSent on every pending notification and persists via the repository; no gateway/provider integration exists yet.

nodes.label: ApplicationDbContext
nodes.rationale: Exposes seven DbSets including LoyaltyTransaction, which is a child of the Customer aggregate - direct set access leaks an aggregate-internal entity for query convenience.

nodes.label: Assembly-Scanned EF Configuration Discovery
nodes.rationale: ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly(Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly()) wires every IEntityTypeConfiguration implicitly, so adding a configuration class requires no DbContext edit - but there is no compile-time link, and a config in another assembly would be silently ignored.

nodes.label: DbSeeder.SeedAsync
nodes.rationale: Builds the demo dataset exclusively through domain factory methods (SalonService.Create, StaffMember.Create, Customer.Create, Booking.Create) instead of object initializers, so invariants and domain events fire exactly as they would at runtime.

nodes.label: Guarded Idempotent Seeding
nodes.rationale: Each section is fenced by an AnyAsync() emptiness check and saved in stages, so the seeder is safe to call on every startup; the sample Booking is nested under the Customers guard, so it is only ever created together with the first customer.

nodes.label: BookingConfiguration
nodes.rationale: Declares only shadow (non-navigational) relationships via HasOne<T>().WithMany() so Booking stays a pure aggregate root holding foreign-key ids rather than object references to other aggregates.

nodes.label: Owned Value-Object Mapping of BookingSlot
nodes.rationale: OwnsOne flattens the BookingSlot value object into SlotDate/SlotStartTime/SlotEndTime columns on the Bookings table, keeping the value object non-identifiable while letting queries filter on b.Slot.Date.

nodes.label: Enum-to-String Column Conversion
nodes.rationale: BookingStatus, WaitlistStatus, ServiceCategory, NotificationChannel and NotificationType are all persisted with HasConversion<string>() and a length cap, so stored data stays readable and survives enum reordering.

nodes.label: Restrict Delete on Cross-Aggregate Foreign Keys
nodes.rationale: Every reference that crosses an aggregate boundary (Booking/Notification/Waitlist to Customer, Staff, Service) uses DeleteBehavior.Restrict so historical bookings can never be silently destroyed by deleting a catalogue row; the one exception is WaitlistEntry.PreferredStaffId which uses SetNull because a staff preference is optional.
nodes.norm_label: restrict delete on cross-aggregate foreign keys

nodes.label: Cascade Delete for Aggregate-Owned Child Collections
nodes.rationale: Collections that live inside an aggregate (Customer.LoyaltyTransactions, StaffMember.WorkingSchedules, StaffMember.TimeOffs) cascade on delete, expressing that they have no life of their own outside the root.
nodes.norm_label: cascade delete for aggregate-owned child collections

nodes.label: CustomerConfiguration
nodes.rationale: PreferredLanguage defaults to "ar" at the database level, encoding Arabic-first localisation as a persistence default rather than application logic.

nodes.label: LoyaltyTransactionConfiguration
nodes.rationale: Second IEntityTypeConfiguration co-located in the Customer configuration file because the entity is part of the Customer aggregate; assembly scanning picks it up regardless of file placement.

nodes.label: NotificationConfiguration
nodes.rationale: Channel and Type are converted to strings but Status is left as a plain length-capped property, an inconsistency with the other enum mappings.

nodes.label: SalonServiceConfiguration
nodes.rationale: Mandates both NameAr and NameEn and gives Price precision(18,2), making bilingual naming a persistence-level invariant of the service catalogue.

nodes.label: StaffMemberConfiguration
nodes.rationale: Maps WorkingSchedules and TimeOffs as cascading child collections keyed by StaffMemberId, defining the staff availability aggregate.

nodes.label: WaitlistEntryConfiguration
nodes.rationale: Uses DeleteBehavior.SetNull for PreferredStaffId (an optional preference) while Customer and Service references stay Restrict, the only place in the model that mixes delete behaviours on one entity.

nodes.label: Repository<T> Generic EF Base
nodes.rationale: Only CRUD primitives live in the generic base (FindAsync/ToListAsync/Add/Update/Remove); every domain-specific query is pushed down to the concrete repository so the base stays free of Include/filter policy. Update/Delete are synchronous bodies returning Task.CompletedTask because EF change tracking needs no await.

nodes.label: BookingRepository
nodes.rationale: Deliberately loads bookings without Include of Customer/Service/Staff: booking queries are used for availability math and lists, where only the owned Slot value object and foreign keys are needed.

nodes.label: NotificationRepository
nodes.rationale: The only repository that does NOT extend Repository<T>: Notification is not an AggregateRoot, so it cannot satisfy the generic constraint. It re-declares its own _context field and exposes only the three operations the outbox-style dispatch loop needs (GetPending / Add / Update), with no GetById or Delete.

nodes.label: StaffRepository
nodes.rationale: Every read path eagerly Includes WorkingSchedules and TimeOffs because the staff aggregate is never useful without its availability calendar - callers compute bookable slots in memory, so a lazy/split load would cause N+1 round trips per staff member.

nodes.label: UnitOfWork (EF SaveChanges wrapper)
nodes.rationale: Thin delegation to DbContext.SaveChangesAsync only. It opens no explicit transaction (relying on EF's implicit per-SaveChanges transaction) and performs NO domain-event dispatch, even though AggregateRoot collects domain events - so events raised by aggregates are never published from the persistence boundary.

nodes.label: WaitlistRepository
nodes.rationale: Ordering encodes queue fairness: waiting entries are ordered ascending by CreatedAt (FIFO offer order) while a customer's own history is ordered descending (newest first).

nodes.label: BookingRepository.GetByStaffAndDateAsync
nodes.rationale: Backs slot-availability / double-booking checks: filters on staff + Slot.Date and explicitly excludes BookingStatus.Cancelled so freed slots become bookable again.

nodes.label: BookingRepository.GetByCustomerIdAsync
nodes.rationale: Backs the customer portal 'my bookings' history; sorts by the owned Slot.Date/StartTime descending rather than CreatedAt so the list reads as an appointment calendar.

nodes.label: BookingRepository.GetAllAsync(from,to)
nodes.rationale: Admin dashboard/reporting window. Note it filters on CreatedAt (when the booking was made), not on Slot.Date (when the appointment happens), and it overloads the base GetAllAsync name.

nodes.label: WaitlistRepository.GetExpiredOffersAsync
nodes.rationale: Hard-codes a 30-minute offer window (DateTime.UtcNow.AddMinutes(-30)) inside the repository rather than taking it as a parameter or from configuration - the expiry policy lives in the persistence layer.

nodes.label: NotificationRepository.GetPendingAsync
nodes.rationale: Dispatch-loop claim query: matches the magic string Status == "Pending" (Status is an untyped string column, not an enum) and caps retries at RetryCount < 3.

nodes.label: StaffRepository.GetByServiceAsync
nodes.rationale: Filters with SpecialtyServiceIds.Contains(serviceId) over a collection property that has no table of its own in the migration - it is persisted as a serialized/owned column, so this predicate is a value-collection match rather than a join.

nodes.label: CustomerRepository.GetByExternalAuthIdAsync
nodes.rationale: Backs external-login account resolution (ExternalAuthId + AuthProvider). Both columns are nullable and carry no index in the InitialCreate migration, so every social sign-in performs a table scan.

nodes.label: CustomerRepository.GetAllAsync(page,pageSize)
nodes.rationale: Pages without an OrderBy and without returning a total count, unlike the Staff/Service paged queries - page boundaries are therefore not deterministic.

nodes.label: InitialCreate Migration
nodes.rationale: Single migration creating the whole schema. Aggregate-to-aggregate FKs use Restrict (no cascade across aggregate boundaries), child collections owned by an aggregate use Cascade, and the optional Waitlist.PreferredStaffId uses SetNull.

nodes.label: Generic Repository + Concrete Specialization Pattern
nodes.rationale: Shared CRUD is inherited once from Repository<T> so each concrete repository only owns the queries its aggregate actually needs, keeping domain interfaces narrow while avoiding five copies of Add/Update/Delete.

nodes.label: Unit-of-Work Save Semantics
nodes.rationale: Repositories never call SaveChanges themselves - they only stage changes on the tracked DbContext, and a single UnitOfWork.SaveChangesAsync at the end of a use case commits them atomically in EF's implicit transaction. No explicit BeginTransaction and no domain-event dispatch hook exist.

nodes.label: Eager Loading of the Staff Availability Graph
nodes.rationale: WorkingSchedules and TimeOffs are Included on every staff query because slot generation needs the full calendar in memory; loading them lazily per staff member would produce N+1 queries on the busiest read path.
nodes.norm_label: eager loading of the staff availability graph

nodes.label: Offset Pagination with Total Count
nodes.rationale: CountAsync on the filtered query followed by Skip/Take on the same IQueryable gives the API a (Items, TotalCount) tuple in two round trips without materializing the whole set.

nodes.label: IsActive Flag as Soft Catalog Visibility
nodes.rationale: Services and staff are never hard-deleted from public reads; every catalog query re-applies Where(x => x.IsActive) by hand instead of a global query filter, so retired rows stay available for historical bookings.
nodes.norm_label: isactive flag as soft catalog visibility

nodes.label: Status+Timestamp Polling Predicate for Background Jobs
nodes.rationale: Both the notification dispatcher and the waitlist expirer claim work by scanning a table for (status marker + bounded age/retry count) rather than using a queue - the recurring Hangfire jobs poll these predicates.
nodes.norm_label: status+timestamp polling predicate for background jobs

nodes.label: Restrict Across Aggregates, Cascade Within
nodes.rationale: Bookings/Waitlist/Notifications reference Customers, Services and Staff with ReferentialAction.Restrict so a referenced aggregate can never be deleted out from under a transaction record, while aggregate-owned children (WorkingSchedule, TimeOff, LoyaltyTransactions) cascade with their parent and the optional Waitlist.PreferredStaffId degrades to SetNull.

nodes.label: Index-per-Foreign-Key Strategy
nodes.rationale: Only EF's automatic FK indexes exist (IX_Bookings_CustomerId/ServiceId/StaffId, IX_Waitlist_*, IX_Notifications_*, IX_TimeOff_StaffMemberId, IX_WorkingSchedule_StaffMemberId). There is no composite (StaffId, Slot.Date) index for the availability query, no index on Booking status or Notification status, and none on Customer.ExternalAuthId.

nodes.label: Depicted Subject: Two Stacked Floating Squircle Slabs
nodes.norm_label: depicted subject: two stacked floating squircle slabs

nodes.label: Outlined Translucent Upper Slab with Dashed Alignment Guides
nodes.norm_label: outlined translucent upper slab with dashed alignment guides

nodes.label: Iridescent Violet-Indigo Gradient Edge on Lower Slab
nodes.norm_label: iridescent violet-indigo gradient edge on lower slab

nodes.label: Isometric Exploded-Layer Composition
nodes.rationale: The subject is drawn as two separated, perfectly aligned layers joined by dashed construction lines. Exploded isometric views read as 'system made of composable parts', a device borrowed from product/SaaS marketing rather than traditional spa photography - it signals that the product is software, not the salon itself.

nodes.label: Minimal White / Transparent Negative-Space Backdrop
nodes.rationale: No background scene, no texture, no text. The subject floats in empty space with thin 1px linework, so the asset can be dropped onto any surface and stays legible at small sizes; it also leaves headline and CTA type as the loudest element of a hero section.

nodes.label: Electric Purple / Violet Brand Accent Palette
nodes.rationale: Purple is the only saturated hue in the image and it is confined to a single edge against otherwise neutral white. Purple carries luxury/beauty connotations while the restraint (one accent, everything else neutral) keeps it premium rather than playful.
nodes.norm_label: electric purple / violet brand accent palette

nodes.label: Premium, Calm, Tech-Modern Mood
nodes.rationale: Soft rounded corners, generous whitespace, a single jewel-toned accent and no human subject produce a quiet, high-end, contemporary tone - positioning the booking product as a polished digital service rather than a discount scheduler.

nodes.label: Visual Identity of the Spa Booking Product
nodes.rationale: The asset encodes the brand contract the rest of the UI inherits: neutral base, one electric-purple accent, rounded geometry, lots of air.
nodes.norm_label: visual identity of the spa booking product

nodes.label: Hero Asset Is Not Imported Anywhere
nodes.rationale: A repo-wide search for 'hero.png' and 'assets/' across frontend/src and index.html returns no import or url() reference. The live hero in Home.css instead uses a remote Unsplash photograph behind a dark overlay, so this file is currently an orphaned/candidate brand asset rather than shipped art.
nodes.norm_label: hero asset is not imported anywhere

nodes.label: Light Asset vs Dark Charcoal App Theme
nodes.rationale: The illustration is white-on-white with dark hairlines, while the shipped theme is dark charcoal (#121212) with light text. Placing this asset in the live hero unchanged would require inversion or a light surface, which may be why the dark photographic hero was used instead.
nodes.norm_label: light asset vs dark charcoal app theme

nodes.label: App Favicon (Vite bolt mark)
nodes.rationale: Serves as the browser-tab mark referenced by frontend/index.html, but the geometry is byte-for-byte the Vite lightning-bolt logo path (purple #863bff / #7e14ff blurred-ellipse glow stack) with the Vite parenthesis glyphs removed. It encodes no spa/salon/reservation brand symbol - it is unrebranded Vite template artwork still shipping as the product's identity.

nodes.label: frontend/index.html (favicon link)
nodes.rationale: The single literal consumer of favicon.svg: <link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="/favicon.svg" />. The same line is mirrored into the built frontend/dist/index.html.

nodes.label: Icon Sprite Sheet (icons.svg)
nodes.rationale: A 6-symbol SVG sprite defining ONLY developer/community affordances (bluesky, discord, documentation, github, social, x) with Vite-purple #aa3bff strokes. It contains no booking, calendar, staff, service, loyalty or payment iconography, and no source file under frontend/ references it - a grep for 'icons.svg' across ts/tsx/html/css/json returns zero hits. It is the Vite React starter landing-page sprite left behind by the scaffold, not the product's UI icon system.

nodes.label: bluesky-clip clipPath
nodes.rationale: Support definition only - a rectangular clip region consumed by bluesky-icon via clip-path=url(#bluesky-clip); carries no product meaning.

nodes.label: documentation-icon symbol
nodes.rationale: Stroked outline of a document with angle-bracket/code marks - reads as 'read the docs', a developer affordance rather than an end-user spa feature.

nodes.label: social-icon symbol
nodes.rationale: A person silhouette with a star badge. Shape-wise it is the closest thing in the sprite to a customer/profile or review/rating affordance, but in the Vite starter it labels the 'join the community' link group - the product reading is unverified.

nodes.label: React Logo (react.svg)
nodes.rationale: Vestigial Vite+React template asset: the iconify #00D8FF React atom logo. No file in the repository imports it; it survives only because the scaffold's default App.tsx once displayed it. Safe to delete.

nodes.label: Vite Logo (vite.svg)
nodes.rationale: Vestigial Vite+React template asset: the Vite wordmark bolt between parentheses, with a prefers-color-scheme dark rule flipping the parenthesis fill. Unreferenced anywhere in the frontend. Its bolt path is the same artwork that favicon.svg ships as the app's tab icon.

nodes.label: Vite + React Template Scaffolding (vestigial)
nodes.rationale: All four SVG assets in this chunk trace back to the `npm create vite` React-TS starter rather than to the reservation product. Three of them (icons.svg, react.svg, vite.svg) have no inbound reference at all; the fourth (favicon.svg) is wired up but still shows Vite's mark.

nodes.label: Browser Tab / Brand Identity
nodes.rationale: The product concept the favicon is supposed to serve. Currently unfulfilled - the tab mark is the framework's logo, so the spa reservation app has no distinct visual identity at the browser-tab level. Flagged as a rebranding gap.

nodes.label: Community / Social Link Affordances
nodes.rationale: Bluesky, Discord, GitHub, X and the person+star glyph together form an outbound social/community link cluster - the affordance set of a framework landing page. A spa booking product would plausibly want Instagram/Facebook/WhatsApp instead, so even if these were adopted they are the wrong social surface.

nodes.label: Developer Documentation Link
nodes.rationale: documentation-icon points at framework docs, an affordance for developers rather than for salon customers or staff.

nodes.label: Booking / Scheduling UI Iconography (absent)
nodes.rationale: Recorded as a negative finding: the sprite defines no calendar, clock, scissors, staff, service, loyalty-points, waitlist or payment symbol. Whatever iconography the booking flow, staff scheduler, customer portal and admin dashboard use must come from an icon library or inline JSX elsewhere in frontend/src, not from this sprite. Any edge asserting icons.svg serves a product flow is unverified and marked AMBIGUOUS.
